arxiv-1909-07224.title: K -essence Emergent Spacetime as Generalized Vaidya Geometry
arxiv-1909-07224.creator: Goutam Manna, Parthasarathi Majumdar, Bivash Majumder
arxiv-1909-07224.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Goutam Manna, Parthasarathi Majumdar, Bivash Majumder. We establish a formal connection between the K -essence emergent gravity scenario and generalizations of Vaidya spacetime. Choosing the K -essence action to be of the Dirac-Born-Infeld variety, the physical spacetime to be a general static spherically symmetric black hole and restricting the K -essence scalar field to be a function solely of the advanced or the retarded time, we show that the emergent gravity metric resembles closely the generalized Vaidya metrics for null fluid collapse proposed by

arxiv-2106-00160.title: Controllability of surface gravity waves and the sloshing problem Thanks: M. A. Fontelos was partially supported by Ministerio de Economía, Industria y Competitividad, Gobierno de España (Grant No. MTM2017–89423–P)
arxiv-2106-00160.creator: M. A. Fontelos, J. López-Ríos
arxiv-2106-00160.description: Abstract . We study the problem of controlling the free surface for a two dimensional solid container in the context of the gravity waves and the sloshing problem. By using conformal maps and the Dirichlet–Neumann operator, the problem is formulated as a second order evolutionary equation on the free surface involving a self-adjoint operator.

arxiv-2205-02074.title: Subexponentiality of densities of infinitely divisible distributions
arxiv-2205-02074.creator: Muneya Matsui
arxiv-2205-02074.description: Abstract . We show the equivalence of three properties for an infinitely divisible distribution: the subexponentiality of the density, the subexponentiality of the density of its Lévy measure and the tail equivalence between the density and its Lévy measure density, under monotonic-type assumptions on the Lévy measure density.

arxiv-2205-05408.title: On the equivariant log-concavity for the cohomology of the flag varieties
arxiv-2205-05408.creator: Tao Gui
arxiv-2205-05408.description: Abstract . We study the S n S_{n} -equivariant log-concavity of the cohomology of flag varieties, also known as the coinvariant ring of S n S_{n} . Using the theory of representation stability, we give computer-assisted proofs of the equivariant log-concavity in low degrees and high degrees and conjecture that it holds for all degrees.

arxiv-2211-09995.title: Contractility-induced phase separation in active solids
arxiv-2211-09995.creator: Sifan Yin, L. Mahadevan
arxiv-2211-09995.description: Abstract A combination of cellular contractility and active phase separation in cell-matrix composites is thought to be an enabler of spatiotemporal patterning in multicellular tissues across scales, from somitogenesis to cartilage condensation. To characterize these phenomena, we provide a general theory that incorporates active cellular contractility into the classical Cahn–Hilliard–Larché model for phase separation in passive viscoelastic solids.

arxiv-2302-00342.title: Bayesian inference for a spatio-temporal model of road traffic collision data
arxiv-2302-00342.creator: Nicola Hewett, Andrew Golightly, Lee Fawcett & Neil Thorpe
arxiv-2302-00342.description: Abstract Improving road safety is hugely important with the number of deaths on the world’s roads remaining unacceptably high; an estimated 1.35 million people die each year (WHO, 2020). Current practice for treating collision hotspots is almost always reactive: once a threshold level of collisions has been exceeded during some predetermined observation period, treatment is applied (e.g. road safety cameras).

arxiv-2303-08615.title: Characteristic Function of the Tsallis q q -Gaussian and Its Applications in Measurement and Metrology Journal: Metrology 2023, 3(2), 222-236; https://doi.org/10.3390/metrology3020012 ,
arxiv-2303-08615.creator: Viktor Witkovský
arxiv-2303-08615.description: Abstract The Tsallis q q -Gaussian distribution is a powerful generalization of the standard Gaussian distribution and is commonly used in various fields, including non-extensive statistical mechanics, financial markets and image processing. It belongs to the q q -distribution family, which is characterized by a non-additive entropy.

arxiv-2502-21165.title: Bayesian Selection for Efficient MLIP Dataset Selection Journal: Modelling Simulation Mater. Sci. Eng.
arxiv-2502-21165.creator: Thomas Rocke, James R. Kermode
arxiv-2502-21165.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Rocke, James R. Kermode. The problem of constructing a dataset for MLIP development which gives the maximum quality in the minimum amount of compute time is complex, and can be approached in a number of ways. We introduce a “Bayesian selection” approach for selecting from a candidate set of structures, and compare the effectiveness of this method against other common approaches in the task of constructing ideal datasets targeting Silicon surface energies.

arxiv-2506-23181.title: Finite size effect in Kuramoto oscillators with inertia on simplicial complex
arxiv-2506-23181.creator: Manuel Lourenço, Abhishek Sharma, Priyanka Rajwani, Erick Alejandro Madrigal Solis, Mehrnaz Anvari, Sarika Jalan
arxiv-2506-23181.description: Abstract We investigate the finite-size effects on the dynamical evolution of the Kuramoto model with inertia coupled through triadic interactions. Our findings reveal that fluctuations resulting from the finite size drive the system toward a synchronized state at finite coupling, which contrasts with the analytical predictions in thermodynamic limit made for the same system.

arxiv-2507-06668.title: A Twisted 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 2 ​ ( ℂ ) \mathfrak{sl}_{2}(\mathbb{C}) Isomonodromic-Isospectral Correspondence Institut Camille Jordan, CNRS UMR 5208, Les Forges 2, 20 Rue du Dr Annino, 42000 Saint-Étienne, France. mohamad.alameddine@univ-st-etienne.fr
arxiv-2507-06668.creator: Mohamad Alameddine
arxiv-2507-06668.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohamad Alameddine. The aim of this article is to generalize the isomonodromic-isospectral correspondence for meromorphic connections of rank 2 2 over ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} to the twisted case. More specifically, the construction of the isospectral approach is provided for the Painlevé I hierarchy, then two maps are constructed, one linking the sets of isomonodromic and isospectral Hamiltonians, another linking the set of apparent singularities to a set of isospectral coordinates.

arxiv-2508-12169.title: A unified method for generating closed-form point estimators for exponential families: An example with the beta distribution applied to proportions of land used for farming
arxiv-2508-12169.creator: Roberto Vila 1 and Helton Saulo 1,2 1 Department of Statistics, University of Brasilia, Brasilia, Brazil 2 Department of Economics, Federal University of Pelotas, Pelotas, Brazil
arxiv-2508-12169.description: Abstract We show that, after a simple power–transform reparameterization of the (vector) exponential family, the solutions to the likelihood equations coincide with moment-type estimating equations. This equivalence enables a unified route to closed-form point estimators for multi-parameter models that typically lack explicit maximum likelihood (ML) solutions.

arxiv-2510-25209.title: On Robust Popular Matchings with Tie-Bounded Preferences and Stable Matchings with Two-Sided Ties
arxiv-2510-25209.creator: Koustav De
arxiv-2510-25209.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Koustav De. We are given a bipartite graph G = ( A ∪ B , E ) G=\left(A\cup B,E\right) . In the one-sided model, every a ∈ A a\in A (often called agents) ranks its neighbours z ∈ N a z\in N_{a} strictly, and no b ∈ B b\in B has any preference order over its neighbours y ∈ N b y\in N_{b} , and vertices in B B abstain from casting their votes to matchings.

arxiv-2601-08968.title: Elasticity without a reference state: continuum mechanics of active tension nets
arxiv-2601-08968.creator: Nikolas H. Claussen, Fridtjof Brauns, Boris I. Shraiman
arxiv-2601-08968.description: Abstract A constitutive relation between stress and strain relative to a reference state is the basic assumption of elasticity theory. However, in living matter, stress is governed by (motor molecule) activity rather than a constitutive law. What paradigm takes the place of elasticity in this setting?

pmc-10514796.title: Improving 2-Chlorotrityl Chloride (2-CTC) Resin Activation
pmc-10514796.creator: Tanya Román, Gerardo Acosta, Beatriz G. de la Torre, Constanza Cárdenas, Fanny Guzmán, Fernando Albericio
pmc-10514796.description: Used in solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) for peptides with an acid termination, the 2-chlorotrityl chloride (2-CTC) resin is highly susceptible to moisture, leading to reduced resin loading and lower synthetic yields. It is therefore recommended that the resin be activated with thionyl chloride (SOCl2) before peptide assembly.

pmc-10583590.title: Comprehensive Analysis of Prognostic Value and Immune Infiltration of TFAP2 Family Members in Bladder Cancer from Database and FFPE Sample
pmc-10583590.creator: Feng Yuan, Yi Sun, Guang-Cheng Dai, Qiu Yao, Yi-bing Zhou, Ya-cheng Zang, Xiao-Long Liu, Bo-Xin Xue
pmc-10583590.description: Background: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is one of the common malignant tumors worldwide. Recent studies have shown that Transcription factor activating protein-2(TFAP2) family proteins plays a bidirectional regulatory role in the process of tumorigenesis versus evolution by regulating the expression of tumor associated genes. However, little is known about the function of distinct TFAP2s proteins in patient with BLCA.

pmc-11371794.title: Group-member selection for RSVP-based collaborative brain-computer interfaces
pmc-11371794.creator: Yuan Si, Zhenyu Wang, Guiying Xu, Zikai Wang, Tianheng Xu, Ting Zhou, Honglin Hu
pmc-11371794.description: ObjectiveThe brain-computer interface (BCI) systems based on rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) have been widely utilized for the detection of target and non-target images. Collaborative brain-computer interface (cBCI) effectively fuses electroencephalogram (EEG) data from multiple users to overcome the limitations of low single-user performance in single-trial event-related potential (ERP) detection in RSVP-based BCI systems.

pmc-12394745.title: Continued Root Formation after a Compound root Fracture in an Immature Permanent Incisor: A Case Report with a 2-year follow-up
pmc-12394745.creator: Maryam Enteghad, Safoora Sahebi, Saleh Hadian
pmc-12394745.description: While traumatic injuries in the young permanent dentition are frequent, root fractures are relatively rare, particularly in immature teeth. This study reports the case of a 7-year-old boy who fell off a bicycle. Radiographic examination showed an immature right upper central incisor with fractures in the middle and along the root in an oblique and horizontal direction.

pmc-12536628.title: Environmental risk assessment of the Cry1B.34.1, Cry1B.61.1, and IPD083Cb proteins to non-target organisms
pmc-12536628.creator: Joseph E. Iboyi, Chad J. Boeckman, Kristine LeRoy, Stephen L. Ballou, Reba J. Bruyere, Verissimo G. de Sá, Timothy Gunderson, Emily Huang, Christopher Linderblood, Taylor Olson, Bridget F. O’Neill, Josh J. Parsons, Mathew Sandmann, Brian Stolte, Yiwei Wang
pmc-12536628.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Lepidopteran pests are a serious threat to soybean production worldwide and have developed resistance to several pest management options, including the use of transgenic soybean expressing crystalline (Cry) proteins derived from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis Berliner (Bt). For this reason, there is great interest in discovering insecticidal proteins that function via new modes and/or sites of action against lepidopteran pests to support a sustainable and durable management plan.

pmc-12568818.title: Are multiple limb injuries in severely injured patients negligible? Evaluation of progression and outcome using a new scoring system for extremity injury: the Extremity Severity Score (ESS)
pmc-12568818.creator: Claudius Thiedemann, Markus Rupp, Anton Heller, Julia Lenz, Ingmar Geiger, Daniel Popp, Volker Alt, Antonio Ernstberger
pmc-12568818.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionExtremity injuries appear to have less impact on the mortality of multiple trauma patients (ISS ≥ 16). The Primary Survey of the Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) only lists pelvic and femur fractures among the extremity injuries. The aim of this study was to evaluate the role of multiple extremity injuries in terms of lethality, progression, and complications in multiple trauma patients and the actual influence of concomitant blood loss.
